turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): come on in, either chair is fine. i'm doctor ellis. that hallway is a maze, huh?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): uh, yeah. i almost bailed in the parking lot. my sister's the one who wanted this.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): because you promised, after my endo appointment. i'm jenna.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): glad you both made it. what's been going on, from your side?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): it's not a big thing. i've lost a bit of weight and my heart speeds up sometimes. she panicked 'cause of her thyroid, not 'cause i'm sick.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): okay. walk me through the weight, however it looks to you.
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): umm, maybe a month. and i eat more than usual, second helpings, so i'm not dieting or anything.
[SEG0008] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): a month? no. she's been dropping since april, that's three months, and the home scale said 128 this morning, down from 142.
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): i'm not fighting the 128. the three months is her story, not mine.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): alright, i'll hold the weight change as roughly one to three months, since you're not landing in the same place. we can leave the exact start open.
[SEG0011] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): she sweats through her shirt by lunch too. even at the library desk.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): okay, i sweat more than i used to. it's summer. can we not make it a whole thing?
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): tell me about the fast heart. what does it feel like?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): pounding. comes and goes. the machine out front said 124 and everybody freaked. i was just sitting there.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): any chest pain with it?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): no. none.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): shortness of breath?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): mm. no, breathing's fine.
[SEG0019] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): her hands shake. her coffee was rippling this morning, i watched it.
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): only a little, and only after coffee. it's not a disease.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): when did the pounding start? even a rough guess.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): err, i don't know. i can't put a date on it. it just showed up.
[SEG0023] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): and she sleeps badly. up at two, up again at four, i hear her.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): i do not. i sleep fine. you just wake up easy and blame me.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): so you two don't agree about the sleep. i'm leaving that one unsettled.
[SEG0026] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): oh, she sliced her thumb on a cat food lid last week. healed in five days. looked totally normal.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): any cuts that have been slow to heal?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): no. that one closed in five days. it was nothing.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): what medicines do you take? only yours, not someone else's.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): um, sertraleen, fifty milligrams, every morning, for the anxiety. been a couple years.
[SEG0031] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): she skips it on sundays. sunday in the pill box is always still full.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): no. saturdays. i miss saturdays when i'm off work. not sundays. she got the day wrong.
[SEG0033] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): fine, saturdays then. and just so it's not on her chart, the biotin gummies are mine for my hair, and my methimazole is for my graves'. she's never taken them.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): right, her thyroid, not mine. i don't take her stuff.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): good. biotin and methimazole stay jenna's. your anxiety has been going those couple of years, and the sertraline is every morning except the saturdays you forget.
[SEG0036] person_4 (NURSE): sorry, quick interrupt. i'm nia from triage. heart rate 124, blood pressure 132 over 78, temperature 98.4, oxygen 99 percent. that's the same 124 she saw out front.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): thanks. that lines up with what you said. hands out flat for me.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): they're gonna be normal.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): there is a fine tremor. your neck doesn't feel big. heart is regular, just fast. skin's warm and a little damp.
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): any fever lately?
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): no.
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): besides the bigger appetite, anything with your stomach or bowels?
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): no. bowels are normal.
[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): smoke at all? how about alcohol?
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): never smoked. a beer on the weekend. coffee is three cups a day, well sometimes four, no, three.
[SEG0046] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): she works the desk at the county library. we also got lost in your parking garage, which i'm still mad about, but that's not why we're here.

[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): thinking out loud, the things on my list are an overactive thyroid, especially with jenna's graves' in the family, or anxiety breaking through the sertraline, or the coffee pushing your pulse. i am not going to conclude this is graves' today. i won't pick one of those until the tests come back.
[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): so i'm ordering a tsh, a free t4, and a cbc, plus an ecg before you leave today. those are set, not a maybe.

[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): front desk will book you back in two weeks for the results. try to ease off the extra coffee till then. if you get real chest pain or you pass out, go to the er instead of waiting.

spec.situation: Younger adult losing weight with a fast heartbeat, sweating, shaky hands, eats more than usual; hair thinning not mentioned; a sister has thyroid disease; blood tests and ECG planned.

traps.happens: A caregiver or relative reports observations ('the cut healed in five days', 'she sleeps badly', 'he does not take the tablets on Sundays'); the patient agrees, disagrees or corrects one point. The nurse also reports a measurement that the patient mentioned before.
traps.label_rule: reported_by follows who said it. A healing cut that healed normally is a negative finding (no slow-healing wounds) or nothing, NOT a symptom. A disputed fact is recorded with certainty disputed or as an uncertainty. A correction replaces the earlier value (Saturday, not Sunday).

features: doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.

third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.

bad.reason: Weight loss and 1-3 months supported, but certainty isn't certain due duration disagreement.
bad.text: Weight loss (category=constitutional, status=present, duration=approximately 1 to 3 months, temporality=current, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

bad.reason: Dose, duration, indication supported, but 'every morning' is inaccurate; she misses Saturdays.
bad.text: sertraline (dose=50 mg, frequency=every morning, duration=approximately 2 years, indication=anxiety, status=currently_used, reported_by=patient)

omissions.text: Sertraline adherence is recorded incompletely/wrongly: patient takes sertraline 50 mg every morning but misses Saturdays when off work (family initially said Sundays, patient corrected to Saturdays).
Weight loss amount was stated by family member as 128 lb this morning, down from 142 lb.
Patient reported eating more than usual/second helpings and specifically said she is not dieting.
Patient reported palpitations/pounding occurring even while sitting; the 124 bpm reading happened while she was just sitting there.
Negative gastrointestinal review is incomplete: patient denied stomach problems in addition to saying bowels are normal.
Coffee intake detail was 'three cups a day, sometimes four, no, three' rather than simply three cups daily.
Patient specifically denied ever taking sister Jenna's biotin gummies or methimazole; doctor confirmed those medications belong to Jenna, not the patient.
Doctor explicitly stated he is not concluding this is Graves' disease today and will not choose among overactive thyroid, anxiety breakthrough, or coffee effect until tests return.
Return precautions were specifically for real chest pain or passing out/fainting.
